project.name: OCECM Workbench
project.full_name: Omitting Contextual Factors in Cognitive Models
project.thesis: When a contextual variable shapes a latent decision parameter, omitting it changes the observed choice law. The residual structure can look like a different, more complex cognitive architecture — so a false complex model can beat a simpler context-aware one in model comparison.
project.what_this_repo_is: Not the paper, and not a running experiment. It is a bounded-autonomy research workbench: agent role prompts, loop protocols, decision gates, registries that track what has actually been shown, plus a proxy simulation, a Lean scaffold and a manuscript stub.

nodes.label: omitted_context_mixture_lemma.md
nodes.what: The one real proof draft in the repo: Lemma 1.1, the omitted-context conditional mixture representation, written as a narrative derivation with assumptions, gaps and counterexample candidates.
nodes.why: The mathematical heart of the project so far. It proves that a context-omitting analyst is fitting a mixture law, which is the object every later model-comparison result is about.
nodes.note: Primary statement conditions on (X, Z). The simpler F(theta|Z) display survives only as Corollary 1.2 under fixed or exogenous trial design — that was the A-006 decision.

nodes.label: proof_review_log.md
nodes.what: Dated proof-attempt records: assumptions used, unsupported steps, counterexample search, decision, next action.

nodes.label: bayesian_comparison_plan.md
nodes.what: The contract keeping two comparisons separate: LOOIC / expected log predictive density for prediction, and Bayes factors under declared priors for model evidence.
nodes.why: The most methodologically opinionated document here. It insists KL dominance implies neither, and forbids the GLM proxy from emitting either.
nodes.note: Recommends leave-one-participant-out, but leaves it as an open PI gate.

nodes.note: No mathlib yet. Adding a probability library is itself a separate reviewable decision.

tour.why: Get the thesis and the shape of the workbench in five minutes. Skim the "start here" list, but do not treat it as a ranking.
The live scientific brief. Results 1-6, the boundary conditions that stop the claim being universal, and the M0-M6 model ladder. Everything downstream refers back here.
How a work cycle runs, what it must read first, and which questions stop it dead and go to the human PI.
The evidence ledger. Six claims, none yet supported — this is what stops the project narrating itself as further along than it is.
Six assumptions, one of them rejected by the PI. Read the decision_status column to see the gate working.
The proof route as a status table: what is under review, what is decision-gated, what has not been stated yet.
The one real proof draft. It establishes that a context-omitting analyst is fitting a mixture law — the object every later comparison result is about.
Why LOOIC and Bayes factors answer different questions, why KL dominance implies neither, and why the fast GLM code is forbidden from reporting either.
The staged path from today's proxies to publishable hierarchical Bayesian models. Milestone 0 is met; 1 through 6 are not.
The theorem as running code: context shifts the mean and the dispersion of latent ambiguity aversion, and no true complexity is present.
The three-way contrast the project turns on — context-omitting simple, context-omitting complex, context-aware simple.
The first real cognitive model, written but not yet fitted. The gap between this file and the milestones is the project's main open work.
The destination. Read the abstract for the intended paper, then note how little prose exists beneath it.
Finish here. Seven structured reports are the clearest record of what has actually been done, including a decision raised and answered across consecutive cycles.
